title: Synthesis, Characterization, and Crystal Structures of M(DO3A) (M = Fe, Gd) and Na[M(DOTA)] (M = Fe, Y, Gd)

synthesis.procedure: Prepared similarly to a published method. A mixture of 15.6 g of H3DO3A (42.3 mmol, corrected for 6% water) and 8.16 g of Gd2O3 (45.1 mmol) in 100 mL of water was heated to 100 °C for 4 h. Most of the oxide dissolved and the pH increased from 3.5 to 7.2. Undissolved solid was removed by centrifugation and the solution was purified by preparative HPLC (C18; 98% water/2% CH3CN). Analytical HPLC indicated <0.05% free Gd(III). The purified product is amorphous and hygroscopic.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous heating; centrifugation; preparative HPLC on Rainin Dynamax C18
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: undissolved oxide removed by centrifugation; HPLC purification. The isolated material is amorphous; a distinct carbonate-containing crystalline adduct is described separately.

properties.summary: Paramagnetic MRI-relaxivity agent. Solution hydration number q = 1.8; 20r1 = 4.8 mM−1 s−1. Inner-sphere relaxivity estimated as 2.9 mM−1 s−1 after subtracting an outer-sphere contribution of 2.0 mM−1 s−1. Calculated spin-only μeff = 7.94 μB. More effective water-proton relaxation than the Fe(III) analogues.

synthesis.procedure: Purified amorphous Gd(DO3A) was obtained as above from H3DO3A (15.6 g, 42.3 mmol) and Gd2O3 (8.16 g, 45.1 mmol) in 100 mL of water at 100 °C for 4 h, followed by HPLC. Aqueous methanolic solutions of Gd(DO3A) to which a drop of saturated aqueous NaCl had been added deposited crystals shown by X-ray analysis to be a 3:1 complex of Gd(DO3A) and Na2CO3 (carbonate is a known contaminant of Gd2O3). Subsequent attempts from 3:1 mixtures of purified Gd(DO3A) and Na2CO3 in aqueous solvents gave mixed amorphous/crystalline material. Another unstable twinned trigonal form crystallized from methanol under an acetone atmosphere.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Crystals of the 3:1 Gd(DO3A)/Na2CO3 heptadecahydrate from aqueous methanol plus a drop of saturated NaCl; later from 3:1 purified Gd(DO3A)/Na2CO3. A separate unstable trigonal form from methanol in an acetone atmosphere was twinned (a = 13.479(3) Å, α = 98.3°, probable R3).

properties.summary: Structurally characterized carbonate adduct of Gd(DO3A). Each Gd is enneacoordinate (N4 plus three carboxyl oxygens plus two carbonate oxygens) with no coordinated water in the crystal. Relaxivity values in Table II refer to the Gd(DO3A) chelate in solution rather than this crystal hydrate.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by reacting Gd2O3 with H4DOTA according to a published method. Yield 80–90%. Elemental analysis matched GdNaC16H26N4O8·5H2O. Crystals for diffraction were grown from water. Isostructural with Na[Y(DOTA)(H2O)]·4H2O and the reported Eu analogue.

synthesis.procedure: Freshly prepared Y(OH)3 was obtained by adding 1.85 mL of 1 N NaOH to YCl3 (0.605 mmol), then raising the pH to 8.5–9.0 with additional NaOH. The gelatinous Y(OH)3 was washed three times with 10 mL of water (centrifugation) and added to H4DOTA (0.605 mmol) in 25.0 mL of water. The suspension dissolved on heating at 90 °C for 10 min. Evaporation to dryness gave a white solid (0.84 g, 100% based on Y). A 0.42 g portion was suspended in 25 mL of ethanol, heated to boiling, and dissolved with 10 mL of water. Acetone (2 mL) was added dropwise to the cooled solution to incipient cloudiness. Cooling to 0 °C gave white crystals within 1 h, which were filtered, washed with 5 mL of acetone–water (3:1) and acetone, and dried in vacuo. Yield 140 mg (30%).
